name: Maryland
summary: Quartered with the arms of the Calvert family (gold and black vertical stripes with a counterchanged diagonal) and the Crossland family (red and white quartered with a cross bottony). It is the only US state flag based on English heraldry.
origin: George Calvert, 1st Baron Baltimore, founded the colony of Maryland; his arms combined his father's Calvert arms and his mother's Crossland arms. The banner was used in the colonial period.

After the Civil War, the Calvert colours had been associated with Unionists and the Crossland colours with Confederate sympathisers; combining them symbolised reconciliation. The flag was adopted officially in 1904.

symbols.name: Calvert quarters
symbols.description: Six vertical gold and black stripes with a diagonal band, counterchanged.
symbols.meaning: The paternal family of the Lords Baltimore.

symbols.name: Crossland quarters
symbols.description: Quartered red and white with a cross bottony counterchanged.
symbols.meaning: The maternal family of George Calvert.

facts: It is the only US state flag based on English heraldry.
The design is hugely popular in Maryland, on clothing, food packaging and tattoos.
The official flagpole finial is a gold cross bottony.
clues: Quarters of black-and-gold stripes and red-and-white crosses.
The only US state flag based on the arms of English noble families.
Its two halves once stood for opposing Civil War sympathies.
